newsitem.title: USA: Texas capitol evacuated by bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: Texas capitol evacuated by bomb threat.

text.p: The Texas capitol, where the state legislature was in session, had to be briefly evacuated Thursday after a bomb threat was delivered by a man who was then arrested, officials said.
Texas Department of Public Safety spokeswoman Linda Heasty said about 1,500 people inside the Capitol building in downtown Austin were forced to evacuate shortly after midday.
They included the members of the Texas House of Representatives and State Senate, she said.
Police went in to check the building for possible explosives but decided the threat was a hoax and allowed legislators and their staff back in, Heasty said.
Officials said an unidentified man went into a state office building and told officials a bomb had been planted inside the Capitol. He was quickly arrested.
"We have him in custody right now but we don't have his identity," Heasty said.
She said a number of state office buildings in Austin had been evacuated by bomb threats in recent weeks.

Officials have said the previous bomb threats may have been linked to a separatist group called the Republic of Texas, which says that Texas is a sovereign nation and that its 1845 annexation into the United States was illegal.
